cues.zh: 那时的计算机长这个样子。那时它们还没有屏幕，而是使用电传打字机，会把你执行的操作实际打印出来。而且，数据既不会存储在磁盘、磁带，也不会存储在 SSD 上。那些设备还要过很久才会被发明出来。数据存储在穿孔卡片上。

cues.en: So when you look at the design of ASCII now, there's a lot of stuff in it. You look at it and you're like, really?
cues.zh: 你看现在 ASCII 的设计，里面东西可多了。你一看就想，真的吗？

cues.en: Like what is all this crap in here? You're like, okay. Now zero, the null character. Any of you see c plus plus developers?
cues.zh: 这里面都是些什么鬼东西？你说，好吧。先是零，空字符。你们有谁见过 C++ 开发者？

cues.en: You've seen null. Right? Null survives today. It's the thing in c that marks the end of a string and if you accidentally go past it, then you can hack into the pentagon and all kinds of fun stuff. Brilliant piece of design there. Then we have start of heading, end of headings, start of text, end of text. Now
cues.zh: 你见过 null 吧？null 至今还活着。它就是 C 里标记字符串结尾的东西，你要是不小心越过了它，就能黑进五角大楼，还有各种好玩的事。真是绝妙的设计。然后是标题开始、标题结束、正文开始、正文结束。现在

cues.en: this was all the bottom block of characters here. These are control codes for mechanical teleprinters.
cues.zh: 这全是下面那一块字符。这些是机械电传打字机的控制码。

cues.en: It's what they were invented for. They were invented to physically control this piece of machinery with all the clunking moving parts on your desk. And if your teleprinter
cues.zh: 它们就是为此发明的。发明它们是为了物理控制这台机器，就是你桌上那堆咔哒作响的活动部件。如果你的电传打字机

cues.en: wanted to send start of heading, you would hold down the control key and you would press a because a is the first letter of the alphabet. So control a would be that. Control b would be that. If your teleprinter was printing stuff and you're like, no no no. Stop. End the text. End the text. You would press control c. And that has survived today.
cues.zh: 想发送标题开始，你会按住 Control 键，再按 A，因为 A 是字母表第一个字母。所以 Control-A 就是那个。Control-B 就是那个。如果你的电传打字机正在打印东西，你说，不不不。停下。结束正文。结束正文。你会按 Control-C。而这个一直沿用至今。

cues.en: And, you know, I had to press control c yesterday because I wrote an infinite loop and some code I was hacking around on. So we have these little relics from the days of teleprinters that still crop up all over the place. End of transmission, inquiry, acknowledgment. Yeah. No big deal.
cues.zh: 你知道，我昨天就不得不按了 Control-C，因为我在瞎折腾的代码里写了个死循环。所以这些来自电传打字机时代的小遗迹，至今还到处冒出来。传输结束、询问、确认。对。没什么大不了的。

cues.en: Bell. If you go on a Windows machine and you type echo space control g and you press enter, it will play ta da dot wav because that's how it interprets the I want to physically ring the bell on my teleprinter.
cues.zh: Bell。如果你在 Windows 机器上输入 echo 空格 control g 然后按回车，它会播放 ta da 点 wav，因为这就是它解释我想在电传打字机上物理敲响铃的方式。

cues.en: Backspace.
cues.zh: Backspace。

cues.en: If your backspace key is broken, you can do backspace by pressing control h on most terminals because that's the same control code. And then we get into the tabs, the line feeds, the vertical tab, the form feed, the carriage return. Now, vertical tab is hilarious because it says move the teleprinter vertically until you hit the next metal tab stop. So if anyone ever says tabs versus spaces, tell them you indent your code with vertical tabs and watch as they go and and look it up and try and figure it out. But the reason why we had these characters is a mechanical teleprinter used a thing called a carriage.
cues.zh: 如果你的退格键坏了，在大多数终端上你可以按 control h 来实现退格，因为是同一个控制码。然后我们进入制表符、换行、垂直制表、换页、回车。垂直制表特别搞笑，因为它说的是垂直移动电传打字机直到碰到下一个金属制表位。所以如果有人说起制表符与空格的争论，告诉他们你用垂直制表符缩进代码，然后看着他们去查资料、试图搞明白。但我们有这些字符的原因是机械电传打字机使用了一个叫字车的东西。

cues.en: And in order to print text,
cues.zh: 为了打印文本，

cues.en: the carriage would print something.
cues.zh: 字车会打印一些东西。

cues.en: And then you would return the carriage to the start of the line. That's a carriage return. And then you would feed the paper through to the next line. Carriage return, line feed. Made sense. Now, teleprinters were a little bit simple. And if you wanted to do bold, what you had to do was return the carriage and then you printed the same line again. And it wouldn't overprint exactly so you could get the pseudo bold effect. So carriage return on its own was useful.
cues.zh: 然后你把字车送回行首。这就是回车。然后你把纸送到下一行。回车、换行。很合理。电传打字机有点简单。如果你想做粗体，你要做的就是送回字车，然后重新打印同一行。它不会完全精确地重叠打印，所以你能得到伪粗体效果。所以单独的回车是有用的。

cues.en: Line feed on its own,
cues.zh: 单独一个换行符，

cues.en: not so much. There were very few scenarios where you wanted to move to the next line without getting to the beginning of the next, character. Now, this has survived today. If you run devices whose ancestry is based on Unix,
cues.zh: 就不太行了。很少有场景是你想移到下一行、却不想回到下一行行首。这个做法一直沿用至今。如果你用的设备血统源自 Unix，

cues.en: so Mac OS, Linux, Android devices,
cues.zh: 比如 Mac OS、Linux、Android 设备，

cues.en: they use a single new line as a line feed. That's the end of a line in a text file. And the reason is that they evolved from Unix and Unix evolved from a system called Maltics. And Maltics was the first computer system ever that had device drivers. It's the first thing ever where they had a way of running a little piece of software that sat between your operating system and the physical hardware on your desk.
cues.zh: 它们用单个换行符作为换行。在文本文件里，这就是一行的结尾。原因在于它们从 Unix 演化而来，而 Unix 又演化自一个叫 Multics 的系统。Multics 是史上第一个有设备驱动程序的计算机系统。也是第一次有办法运行一小段软件，夹在你的操作系统和桌上的物理硬件之间。

cues.en: And so they had a place where they could put in this hack to say, if you see a new line, that means also do a carriage return and translate that character and go to the start of the next line. Windows
cues.zh: 于是他们有个地方可以加入这个 hack：如果看到换行符，就意味着同时做一次回车，转换那个字符，并转到下一行开头。Windows

cues.en: 11 has evolved from Windows 10, from Windows eight, seven, five, XP,
cues.zh: 11 从 Windows 10、Windows 8、7、5、XP 演化而来，

cues.en: Vista, 3.1,
cues.zh: Vista、3.1，

cues.en: all the way back to MS DOS which evolved from CPM which was designed to run on really cheap mini computers that did not have device drivers. And so for those early early systems which are ancestors of Microsoft Windows, you had to send a carriage return and a line feed. Otherwise, your return... Your carriage would fall off the end of your teleprinter.
cues.zh: 一路追溯到 MS-DOS，它又演化自 CP/M；CP/M 是为运行在非常便宜、没有设备驱动程序的小型机上而设计的。所以对那些早期早期系统——Microsoft Windows 的祖先——你必须发送回车和换行。否则，你的回车……你的字车会从电传打字机末端掉出去。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: there are some very neat ideas in the next block of ASCII here. One of the decisions that the designers of ASCII had to make is they're like, what punctuation do we actually need? Now if any of you here has ever worked in printer and typesetting,
cues.zh: 在接下来的这部分 ASCII 码中，有一些非常巧妙的设计。ASCII 的设计者们当年必须面对的一个抉择就是：我们到底真正需要哪些标点符号？在座的如果有谁从事过印刷和排版，就会知道

cues.en: we have a minus sign and we have a hyphen and we have an en dash and we have an em dash and these are all different characters
cues.zh: 减号、连字符、en dash 和 em dash 都是完全不同的字符，

cues.en: if you are printing books and printing scientific papers.
cues.zh: 如果你要印刷书籍和科学论文的话。

cues.en: The creators of ASCII were like, no. We don't actually have space for all of these. They kind of look the same anyway. We're just minus sign is a hyphen is a dash. That can double up on all those. But within the last couple of a couple of years, maybe the last decade or so, we've started seeing a resurgence of digital typography because we have retina displays.
cues.zh: 但 ASCII 的创造者们觉得：不行，我们根本没空间放下所有这些字符。反正它们看起来都差不多，干脆让减号兼作连字符和破折号，一个字符顶多个用。不过在过去几年，大概最近十年里，由于 Retina 视网膜屏的普及，数字排版艺术又迎来了复兴。

cues.en: And we have people reading books on Kindles and iPads. And so we're starting to see things like, you know, smart curly quotes and typographers dashes and these things coming back in. Now,
cues.zh: 人们开始用 Kindle 和 iPad 看书。于是我们开始看到弯引号、专业排版破折号等符号又重新回归了。那么，

cues.en: this block here, the decimal digits. One of the most common things that you had to do on a computer was to turn a number into the string that represents that number and back again. And the way you do this in ASCII is you just ignore the top half. You take the bottom four bits of that number and that is the numeric value of the digit that it represents. And this was blisteringly quick. Even on a four bit processor,
cues.zh: 再看这里的十进制数字区域。当年在计算机上最常见的操作之一，就是把数字转成对应的字符串，或者反向转换。而在 ASCII 中，做法极其简单，直接忽略高位即可。取出低 4 位，就是它所代表的实际数值。这种处理速度极快，即便在 4 位处理器上，

cues.en: this was really really quick and easy to do. Now, have you ever looked at ASCII and thought, why is uppercase a 65
cues.zh: 也能非常非常快速轻松地搞定。那么，大家看 ASCII 时有没有想过，为什么大写 A 是 65，

cues.en: and lowercase a is 97? Why would they have picked those numbers to represent the beginning of the Latin alphabet? Well, turns out that those differ by a single bit.
cues.zh: 而小写 a 却是 97？他们为什么选这两个数字作为拉丁字母表的开头？其实，它们之间只相差了一个 bit。

cues.en: So if you want to do a case insensitive string comparison in ASCII, all you do is you ignore the sixth bit and then the values of those are the same and so you can collate based on the the numeric value that you have left. Finally, we mop up a little bit more punctuation and we get to character number one twenty seven right down the end here and that is delete.
cues.zh: 所以，如果你想对 ASCII 字符串进行不区分大小写的比较，只要忽略第六位，剩下的值就相同了。这样一来，就可以根据剩下的数值进行排序。最后，我们再处理一些标点符号，就到了末尾的字符编号 127，也就是 Delete。

cues.en: One one one one one one. Do you know why that is delete?
cues.zh: 1 1 1 1 1 1。你知道为什么这代表 Delete 吗？

cues.en: Imagine you're storing data on a punch card and, you've punched some holes in it that represent your bank records. And now you're like, I need to erase the bank records. Now you could take the card outside and burn it or you can punch through the rest of the holes so you can't see what the data on the... In the first place was.
cues.zh: 想象一下，你把数据存储在打孔卡上，卡上打了些孔，记录着你的银行信息。现在你想把这些记录擦掉。你可以把卡拿到外面烧掉，也可以把剩下的孔全打穿，这样就看不出原来的数据了。

cues.en: Now at this point, YouTube steps in and says, delete was never intended for punch cards. And, I dug into this and actually, it turns out they're right. If you deleted a punch card, ended you up with a thing called a lace card which would fall apart and jam up your mainframe and everyone would be very unhappy with you.
cues.zh: 这时候，YouTube 出面说：Delete 从来就不是为打孔卡设计的。我深入查了一下，结果发现他们说得没错。要是你用 Delete 处理打孔卡，就会弄出一种叫“花边卡”的东西，它会散架，还会卡住主机，所有人都会对你很不满。

cues.en: So yeah, pretty pretty pleased with sugar on it. If you're gonna talk about computing history, do your research. Thank you, YouTube. They're right. I was wrong. It was actually for these. It was for erasing paper tape. So delete was predominantly used for... And if you look at the left hand side of the teleprinter there, you can actually see a paper tape punch machine on the left there. So America pats itself on the back. They're like, that's it. 127
cues.zh: 所以啊，真是谢天谢地。要聊计算机历史，就先做好研究。谢谢你，YouTube。你们说得对，我错了。它其实是用来擦除纸带的。Delete 主要用在……你看电传打字机的左侧，那里就能看到一台纸带打孔机。所以美国人拍拍自己的肩膀，说：成了，127

cues.en: characters is all you're ever going to need. And they give themselves, yeah, we fixed the problem of encoding text and the rest of the world goes, sorry, you did what?
cues.zh: 个字符就是你永远需要的全部字符。然后他们觉得自己解决了文本编码问题，世界其他地方却说：等等，你们刚才说什么？

cues.en: Like, we can't use this. You can't... You haven't even read any of our alphabet.
cues.zh: 就像，我们没法用这个。你连我们的字母表都没读全。

cues.en: Now, for some cultures,
cues.zh: 现在，对于一些文化来说，

cues.en: ASCII was a complete non starter. I think for most cultures, know, Chinese,
cues.zh: ASCII 完全行不通。我想对大多数文化来说，比如中文、

cues.en: Japanese, Kanji, Korean, Thai, Vietnamese,
cues.zh: 日文、汉字、韩文、泰文、越南文、

cues.en: Arabic, Cyrillic. There are cultures that are thousands of years old all over this planet for whom ASCII was like, alright, you kids have fun. This isn't gonna work for us.
cues.zh: 阿拉伯文、西里尔文。这个星球上有很多拥有数千年历史的文化，对它们来说，ASCII 就像是在说：行了，你们这些小孩子玩得开心点吧。这对我们没用。

cues.en: But for quite a lot of cultures, ASCII was sort of almost good enough. It wasn't there but it it came close. Now, my personal journey with plain text
cues.zh: 但对相当多的文化来说，ASCII 算是差不多够用了。它并不完全够，但已经很接近了。现在说说我个人使用纯文本的经历，

cues.en: started in 1988.
I grew up in Zimbabwe where I spoke English and the currency there was dollars and cents. So when I was playing little programs on my my dad's Amstrad,
cues.zh: 我在津巴布韦长大，那里我说英语，货币是美元和美分。所以当我在爸爸的 Amstrad 上运行一些小程序时，

cues.en: it worked. All the characters that I knew about were in the ASCII that ran on the Amstrad one two eight. But then I moved to The UK and I did some homework on the computer. It's a two eight six PC with a... An Epson dot matrix printer.
cues.zh: 一切正常。Amstrad 128 上运行的 ASCII 包含了我认识的所有字符。但后来我搬到了英国，在电脑上做作业。那是一台 286 PC，配着一台……Epson 点阵打印机。

cues.en: And I tried to print this
cues.zh: 我试着打印这个字符，

cues.en: and it didn't work.
cues.zh: 结果失败了。

cues.en: And it didn't work because this is not one of the characters that the Americans cared about in 1965
cues.zh: 之所以失败，是因为这不是 1965 年美国人关心的字符之一，

cues.en: and so it's not part of ASCII.
cues.zh: 所以它不属于 ASCII。

cues.en: And now what had happened is after ASCII was published,
cues.zh: 而 ASCII 发布之后发生的事情是，

cues.en: a lot of people, a lot of companies all over the world, they looked at this and went, well, hang on. ASCII is only seven bits. Is anyone anyone using this bit?
cues.zh: 世界各地有很多人、很多公司看到它后就想：等等。ASCII 只有 7 位。有人在用这一位吗？

cues.en: And of course, nobody said, there's an international standard because there wasn't. And so lots and lots of different people and companies, they jumped in and went, oh, we can use that bit to solve our problem.
cues.zh: 当然，也没人说这里有国际标准，因为当时根本就没有。于是许许多多的人和公司纷纷入局，心想：噢，我们可以拿那部分来解决我们的问题。

cues.en: And this is... If you've ever come across the idea of something called a code page.
cues.zh: 而这个……如果你听说过所谓的代码页这个概念。

cues.en: A code page is a set of rules for saying what the top half of ASCII means
cues.zh: 代码页是一套规则，用来定义ASCII上半部分所代表的含义。

cues.en: on this computer, in this program, in this document,
cues.zh: 在这台电脑上，在这个程序中，在这份文档里，

cues.en: right now, while I'm looking at it. And the reason I couldn't print my homework is that the printer which was less than a meter away connected by a cable was using a different code page to WordPerfect which is what I was using to to do the writing in. Now one of the most popular code pages, one that has become ubiquitous was this one. This is code page four three seven which was the default code page on the IBM PC.
cues.zh: 就在我看着它的时候。我无法打印作业的原因是，不到一米外通过电缆连接的打印机使用了与WordPerfect不同的代码页，而我当时正是用WordPerfect来写作业的。现在最流行的代码页之一，一个已经无处不在的代码页，就是这个。这是代码页437，它是IBM PC上的默认代码页。

cues.en: Now they kept the regular block of ASCII. The top half there,
cues.zh: 现在他们保留了常规的 ASCII 块。就是上面那半部分，

cues.en: they added
cues.zh: 他们添加了

cues.en: most of the characters that were necessary for Northern And Western Europe. They added box drawing characters so you could do little menus and GUIs.
cues.zh: 涵盖了北欧和西欧所需的大部分字符。他们还加入了制表符（box drawing 字符），这样你就能画出简单的菜单和图形界面。

cues.en: And then they added half of the Greek alphabet.
cues.zh: 然后他们又加了半个希腊字母表。

cues.en: Do you know why?
cues.zh: 你知道为什么吗？

cues.en: They took the ones that were used in maths and physics.
cues.zh: 他们直接借用了数学和物理里的那些。

cues.en: There's not enough Greek here to write Greek but there is enough Greek in here to do the most common mathematical and physical formulae and, they didn't have a whole lot of space to work with. They could have put in the whole Greek alphabet but they were not... We'll put in the ones that are in the physics textbooks and the rest you're just kinda gonna have to figure out later. But they also
cues.zh: 这里的希腊字母不够写希腊文，但足够应付最常见的数学和物理公式了，而且他们当时可用的空间也不多。他们本可以把整个希腊字母表都放进去，但他们没有……我们只放物理教科书里出现的那几个，剩下的你就得以后自己慢慢琢磨了。但他们还

cues.en: said, well, we're not running on mechanical teleprinters anymore. Maybe we could use this top section for, little smiley faces and musical symbols and this kind of stuff. And if you've ever seen an IBM PC crash really, really hard, which they used to do quite a lot, you've got a screen full of smiley faces and playing cards and nonsense. And that's because the operating system was churning out control codes which are basically trying to say to the teleprinter, hey, stop. Stop what you're doing. And the screen is going, oh yeah, smiley faces. How nice.
cues.zh: 我说，我们早就不用机械电传打字机了。也许可以把顶部这块区域用来显示小笑脸和音乐符号之类的东西。如果你见过IBM PC彻底崩溃的样子——它们以前经常这样——屏幕上会满是笑脸、扑克牌和乱七八糟的符号。这是因为操作系统在不停地输出控制码，本质上是在试图对电传打字机说：嘿，停下。停下你正在做的事。而屏幕却在想：哦好啊，笑脸。真不错。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: there was a code page created by ANSI, the national... American National Standards Institution
cues.zh: ANSI，也就是美国国家标准学会，曾做过一个代码页，

cues.en: for doing Cyrillic, is the alphabet used to write Russian, Ukrainian, Bulgarian.
cues.zh: 用来支持西里尔字母，也就是俄语、乌克兰语、保加利亚语用的字母系统。

cues.en: And it looked like this, but it didn't work very well because of a historical quirk of encoding systems.
cues.zh: 它大概长这样，但因为编码系统历史遗留的一些奇葩特性，实际效果非常差。

cues.en: It was quite common. You would take a word like, Privyet, which is, hey, hello in Russian. And you'd turn this into this set of numbers according to the code page. But quite a lot of systems would ignore the eighth bit. They would strip it off because they're like, oh no, ASCII is only a seven bit system. Some things use the eighth bit for things.
cues.zh: 当时很常见的情况是：比如你输入 Privyet，也就是俄语里的“你好”，按代码页转换成一组数字，但很多系统会直接忽略第 8 位，把它硬生生剥掉，因为它们觉得“ASCII 明明只是 7 位的系统”；而且有些程序还会把第 8 位挪作他用。
